activities.description: 'Winner' inhales deeply from a cloud labeled 'SUCCESS.'
Two dice appear and fall, then a baby crawls toward them.
The baby grows, climbs a ladder, encounters obstacles, and reaches the top. 'Loser' crawls toward dice at the bottom of the ladder.

characterInteraction.description: No direct interaction; 'Winner' is shown above while 'Loser' remains at the bottom, highlighting the disparity.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The snake wrapping around the ladder symbolizes the hidden obstacles and challenges faced by those with less privilege.

mood.description: Pensive, transitioning to slightly negative. Initially, the visuals depict success, but then shift to illustrate how luck and privilege play a role.

narrativeProgression.description: Explanation of meritocratic hubris as forgetting the role of luck and privilege in success, and implying those less fortunate deserve their fate.

props.name: Two dice, ladder, books (labeled 'Education,' 'Private Education,' 'Private'), images of a school crest, a man in a top hat climbing the ladder, a snake, text labels ('Silver Spoon,' 'The Old School Tie').

scenes.title: Meritocracy and the Role of Luck

activities.description: A hand picks a straw from a group of straws labeled 'Draw Lots'. Three people and a baby walk on a tightrope. 'Winner' spreads his arms as if claiming the whole 'SUCCESS' cloud.

The hand draws a dollar sign with the snake on the ladder. Crosses are drawn over drawings of 'GIFT' and 'LUCK.' 'Loser' is shown in the rain in front of a Jobcentre. Three men with smug expressions are depicted as snakes on a US flag.

characterInteraction.description: No direct interaction, but the scene juxtaposes the success of 'Winner' with the struggles of 'Loser,' highlighting the consequences of the meritocratic system.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The phrase 'There but for the grace of God go I' is shown crossed out, suggesting a shift away from acknowledging the role of chance in life.

mood.description: Pensive, transitioning to increasingly negative as the scene progresses. The visuals highlight the randomness of fate and the harsh consequences of a purely meritocratic system.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Introduction of the dollar sign and crosses, symbolizing the denial of gift, grace, and luck.
Depiction of 'Loser' struggling in the rain, emphasizing the harsh reality of those deemed 'failures.'

narrativeProgression.description: The scene explores the contrast between acknowledging the role of chance in life and the harsh realities of a purely meritocratic system. It then highlights the demoralizing effects of meritocratic beliefs on those who struggle.

scenes.thematicElements: Meritocracy, chance, fate, success, failure, social responsibility.
scenes.title: Chance and the Meritocratic System

activities.description: 'Loser' stands in front of a Jobcentre in the rain. A projection screen appears, and bottles labeled 'RESENTMENT' pour red liquid onto a US flag.

The screen shows the words 'YOUR FAILURE IS YOUR OWN DOING,' and three 'Elite Politicians' stand behind it. A speech bubble reads 'You simply lack the talent and drive to succeed.' Crosses appear on the flag and screen. A bus filled with people labeled 'Resentful' drives by.

A scale appears with 'BOTTOM' and 'TOP' labels and figures representing 'Loser' and 'Winner'. The scale tips. Two figures labeled 'WINNERS' and 'LOSERS' are shown on a snake. Red lines are drawn, and chains appear, connecting common values and social bonds to meritocracy. The entire scene is transformed into a board game with snakes and ladders.

characterInteraction.description: The scene shows 'Loser' being subjected to the demoralizing messages perpetuated by the 'Elite Politicians', highlighting the power dynamic and its impact on individuals.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The chains connecting common values and social bonds to meritocracy visualize how these essential elements are being eroded by a purely merit-based system.

mood.description: Angry, frustrated, and ultimately disheartening. The visuals illustrate the anger and resentment fueled by meritocratic systems, emphasizing the societal divisions they create.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Introduction of the rain and 'RESENTMENT' bottles, signaling a shift towards a more negative mood.
'Elite Politicians' depicted as snakes reinforce the negative mood and emphasize their role in perpetuating harmful beliefs.

narrativeProgression.description: The scene reveals the consequences of meritocratic beliefs for those deemed 'failures,' culminating in a depiction of societal division and the breakdown of social bonds.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Maritocratic hubris.
This is the tendency of winners to inhale too deeply of their success.
To forget the luck and good fortune that helped them on their way.
It's the smug conviction of those who land on top that they deserve their fate.
And by implication that those on the bottom deserve theirs too.
The lightly sense of the contingency of our lot
conduces to a certain humility.
The idea that there but for the grace of God or the accidents of fortune go I.
But a perfect meritocracy banishes all sense of gift or grace or luck.
It diminishes our capacity to see ourselves as sharing a common fate.
And so it leaves little room for the solidarity that can arise when we reflect on the contingency
of our talents and fortunes.
This is what makes merit a kind of tyranny.
Now seen from below the hubris of elites is galling.
No one likes to be looked down upon.
But the meritocratic faith adds insult to injury.
The notion that your fate is in your hands, that you can make it if you try is a double-edged
sword, inspiring in one way, but in videos in another.
It congratulates the winners, but denigrates the losers even in their own eyes.
For those who can't find work or make ends meet, it's hard to escape the demoralizing thought
that their failure is their own doing.
That they simply lack the talent and drive to succeed.
This gives rise to a politics of humiliation.
It combines resentment of the winners with nagging self-doubt.
It's a potent ingredient in the volatile brew of anger and resentment that fuels populist
protest.
To reinvigorate democratic politics, we need to find our way to a morally more robust
public discourse, one that takes seriously the corrosive effect of meritocratic striving
on the social bonds that constitute our common life.
Disentangling the intolerant aspects of populist protest from its legitimate grievances is no
easy matter, but it is important to try.
You're standing these grievances, and creating a politics that can respond to them is the
most pressing political challenge of our time.

youtube_description:
Work hard, play by the rules, and you’ll go as far as your talents will take you. Right? But so often this isn’t how the system works. In this powerful new RSA Minimate, political philosopher Michael Sandel confronts our age of stalling social mobility and entrenched inequality, and asks: what would it take to give everyone a fair shot at a good life?

The minds behind the award-winning RSA Animate series are back! RSA Minimates are super-short, information-packed animations for busy people. All audio excerpts are taken from live, FREE events at the RSA’s HQ in London, and animated by Cognitive. This animation was produced by RSA Senior Events and Animations Producer, Abi Stephenson.

Find out more in Michael's RSA talk here: https://youtu.be/LCZhA-_1n4E
